verdict.rationale: LangGraph natively documents durable execution: agents persist through failures and resume where they left off, checkpointers write exact graph state (even in error states), and a Postgres-backed checkpointer is recommended for production. That implies state survives outside the process, but the evidence never explicitly shows resumption after a process restart or a redeploy. missing for 10: explicit documentation of resuming runs after process restarts and deploys, any evidence of durable-execution integrations (e.g., external workflow engines), independent hands-on corroboration of crash/restart recovery.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can run long-lived agents durably across process restarts and deploys, natively or via durable-execution integrations

citations.quote: Durable execution — Build agents that persist through failures and can run for extended periods, automatically resuming from exactly where they left off.
Checkpointing keeps your place: the checkpointer writes the exact graph state so you can resume later, even when in an error state.
In production, use a checkpointer backed by a database: from langgraph.checkpoint.postgres import PostgresSaver
Use them for short-term, thread-scoped memory, including conversation continuity, human-in-the-loop workflows, time travel, and fault tolerance.
